tools_helpful.evidence: Turn 47/52 — native dotnet build surfaced the two blocking compile errors (CS0104, WMC0909) and confirmed the fix; build succeeded on the 2nd attempt.
Bulk Windows.UI.Xaml -> Microsoft.UI.Xaml rewrite produced a project that compiled after only two manual fixes.

tool_limitations.limitation: Gates on a clean build but does not pre-scan for the DispatcherQueue/Windows.System ambiguity or x:Bind DataTemplate DataType-resolution traps; both surface only as raw compiler errors the agent must interpret unaided.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Documentation is the higher-leverage fix here since the compiler already emits the codes; the missing piece is the replacement guidance, not detection.

failed_apis.why_tried: Direct port of UWP CoreDispatcher.RunAsync priority overload into WinUI 3.
failed_apis.root_cause: File had both `using Windows.System;` (for Windows.System.User APIs central to UserInfo) and `using Microsoft.UI.Dispatching;`, so `DispatcherQueue` and `DispatcherQueuePriority` were ambiguous between Windows.System.* (WinRT) and Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.* (WinUI 3).
failed_apis.fix: Remove `using Microsoft.UI.Dispatching;`, drop the redundant `DispatcherQueuePriority` argument (or fully-qualify Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueue). WinUI 3's DispatcherQueue instance is inherited from Page/Window, so the instance method resolves without the Dispatching using at all.

failed_apis.api: x:Bind inside a DataTemplate with x:DataType="local:Scenario"
failed_apis.why_tried: Preserved the UWP SDK-sample scenario-list ListBox template that binds each Scenario item via compiled binding.
failed_apis.root_cause: WMC0909 'Cannot resolve DataType local:Scenario' — the compiled binding could not resolve the `local:` prefix to the CLR namespace where the `Scenario` type lives after migration, which then cascaded to WMC1111 (x:Bind requires a resolvable x:DataType) and a WMC9999 internal error.
failed_apis.fix: Either point the `local:` xmlns at the namespace that actually declares Scenario (post-rewrite the app's own namespace) and keep x:Bind, or switch the template to classic `{Binding Title}`, which needs no compile-time DataType. Agent chose {Binding}.

doc_errors.wrong: States the CS0104 ambiguity pattern applies to 'any type name that exists in both Windows.UI.Xaml.* and Microsoft.UI.Xaml.*' — scoping it to the Xaml namespaces only.
doc_errors.correct: The same CS0104 trap also fires between Windows.System.* and Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.* for DispatcherQueue / DispatcherQueuePriority — a very common pairing because migrated code frequently keeps `using Windows.System;`.

doc_errors.wrong: Attributes WMC0909/WMC1111/WMC9999 exclusively to an orphaned code-behind (missing sibling .xaml).
doc_errors.correct: The same codes also fire when the .xaml IS present but a DataTemplate's x:Bind uses an x:DataType the compiler cannot resolve — a distinct root cause with a distinct fix.

special_apis.special_handling: These stay in Windows.System (WinRT) after migration and are the reason a UserInfo-style app keeps `using Windows.System;`, which is precisely what collides with Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueue.

errors_encountered.error: CS0104: 'DispatcherQueuePriority' is an ambiguous reference between 'Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueuePriority' and 'Windows.System.DispatcherQueuePriority' (x5)
errors_encountered.root_cause: Both `using Windows.System;` and `using Microsoft.UI.Dispatching;` in scope.
errors_encountered.fix: Drop the Microsoft.UI.Dispatching using and the priority arg; use the inherited DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue(() => ...).

errors_encountered.error: WMC0909 Cannot resolve DataType local:Scenario; WMC1111 DataTemplates containing x:Bind need a DataType; WMC9999 internal error
errors_encountered.root_cause: x:Bind DataTemplate whose x:DataType type could not be resolved via the XAML xmlns prefixes.
errors_encountered.fix: Resolve the local: prefix to Scenario's real namespace and keep x:Bind, or fall back to {Binding}.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: First `dotnet build` failed with 8 errors: 5x CS0104 DispatcherQueuePriority ambiguity + WMC0909/WMC1111/WMC9999 on the scenario-list DataTemplate.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: ~5 turns (47-52), one build failure then a clean rebuild.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Two namespace/binding traps not documented in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md: DispatcherQueue ambiguity with Windows.System, and WMC0909 from an unresolved x:Bind x:DataType.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Agent removed the Dispatching using + priority arg, and switched the DataTemplate from x:Bind/x:DataType to {Binding}. Rebuild succeeded.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Documenting both traps in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md (threading section + x:Bind/orphaned-XAML sections) so the agent applies the fix on the first pass instead of rediscovering it.

env_issues.issue: WinUI 3 window screenshots captured blank in the non-interactive session (composition capture limitation).
env_issues.workaround: Evaluation relied on the UIA tree + behavioral output text; this is an eval-environment caveat, not a migration defect, and is out of scope for the migration skill.
